header: THE PRIORITY DESK. Four kinds of news must stand first on the news tabs, whatever else is in the feeds: DEMISE the death of a renowned person, from West Bengal first, then India, then the world; ACCIDENT a big accident, in a steel plant or anywhere else, in West Bengal first, then India (an accident outside India is not covered); MASSACRE a mass killing, anywhere in the world: a terror attack, a mass shooting, a bombing or air strike, a communal massacre, with at least MASSACRE_DEAD dead (see massacreOf); VISIT a diplomatic visit: the Prime Minister of India abroad (talks, a summit, a state visit), or a foreign head of state or government, minister or delegation visiting India (see visitOf). A story stands first in the ENGLISH, the HINDI or the BENGALI tab according to the language it arrived in, and ONCE: the same news in another language is left out of that language's tab, as the owner asked (only the first to arrive is shown; see assignDesk). The Business tab has a third kind, RECORD: a record high or low of the share market, of gold or silver, or of the dollar against the rupee (see recordMove). HOW I TELL. By the words of the headline, in the three languages; this is a heuristic, not understanding, and I said so wherever it shows. The words are in ONE place below. What each rule needs:

- a demise needs a word that says a death was announced (dies, passes away, निधन, প্রয়াত) AND a word that says the person is somebody (actor, former minister, legend, MP, अभिनेता, पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री, প্রাক্তন, অভিনেতা ...): "man dies in road accident" is not a demise, "veteran actor dies" is. A headline that says only that a death was announced stays an ordinary story.

- an accident needs a word of accident (blast, collapse, fire, crash, derail, gas leak, हादसा, বিস্ফোরণ ...) AND a sign that it is BIG: at least THREE people dead (a number beside killed/dead/died), or a word of disaster (tragedy, major, massive, devastating), or any accident at a steel plant (a steel plant's accident is news to this plant, big or small).

- where: West Bengal if the headline names it (Bengal, Kolkata, Durgapur, Asansol ... or Bengali writing about a Bengal place); the world if it names a foreign country or city and no Indian place; else India. Bengali script alone does not make a story West Bengal's: the Bengali papers carry the national and world desks too.

ONE STORY ONCE, ACROSS LANGUAGES. A death or an accident is told in three scripts, so the headlines share no words. I match them by the NAMES in them, written in sound: each name is reduced to a skeleton of its consonants (Dharmendra, धर्मेंद्र and ধর্মেন্দ্র all give the same one), and two stories of one kind, within 36 hours, are the same when they share a skeleton that few headlines of the batch carry (a name, a place), or two shorter ones (the same number of dead counts as one for an accident). This is a heuristic too; it errs toward showing a story twice rather than hiding a different one (a name has to match, not a common word).

symbols.name: WORLD

symbols.name: scopeOf
doc: Where a story is: West Bengal if it names a place of it; the world if it names a foreign place and no Indian one; else India (the papers are Indian: what names nothing is theirs).

symbols.name: deadCount

symbols.name: visitOf
symbols.sig: export function visitOf(title: string): PriorityFlag | null
doc: Is this a DIPLOMATIC VISIT of note? By the words of the headline (a heuristic, like the others), in three shapes:

- a FOREIGN head of state or government, minister or delegation VISITING INDIA (scope "india"): a word of a visit to India and a title or a leader's name ("Putin to visit India next month", "Japan PM arrives in Delhi");
- a foreign leader MEETING India's Prime Minister AT HOME, in Delhi or another big city ("Sri Lankan President holds talks with PM Modi in New Delhi"): scope "india";

- the Prime Minister of India ABROAD (scope "world"): his name or title, a foreign country, city or leader, and a word of a journey ("PM Modi leaves for Moscow", "Modi to attend G20 summit in Johannesburg") or of talks ("Modi, Putin hold talks at Kremlin"; "PM Modi meets Australian PM").

Not these: a phone or video call; a domestic occasion (a rally, a border post, an inauguration); a cricket match with a foreign team; Nirav or Lalit Modi; India Gate; a domestic visitor, who names no foreign title or leader.

symbols.name: priorityOf
symbols.sig: export function priorityOf(title: string): PriorityFlag | null
doc: The priority of a headline for the three news tabs, or null. A demise first (a renowned person who died in an accident is a demise), then an accident, then a massacre, then a diplomatic visit.

symbols.name: SCOPE_RANK
symbols.sig: const SCOPE_RANK: Record<PriorityScope, number> = { wb: 0, india: 1, world: 2 }
doc: The order of the priority block: West Bengal, then India, then the world; within a scope the newest first.

symbols.name: skeleton
doc: A word reduced to the skeleton of its consonants, in sound: aspirates and the pairs a transliteration mixes up (t/d, k/g/c, b/p/f/v/w, j/z, s/sh) are one letter, vowels and h are dropped, doubles are one.

symbols.name: nameKeys
doc: The words of a headline that may be a name or a place: every capitalised word of the Latin script, and every word of Hindi and Bengali; each as its skeleton, kept when it has three consonants or more.

symbols.name: STOP
doc: The capitalised words that are not names: the days, the months, the words of a headline.

symbols.name: ms
doc: The time of a story, in milliseconds, or NaN.

symbols.name: MAJOR_PAPERS
doc: MAJOR NEWS: the exception to "a story stands in one tab only" (the owner: the death of an eminent person and any huge massacre may stand in more than one tab at once, by their gravity; and the same for any super important news). A story is MAJOR by one of these signs:

- THE DEATH OF AN EMINENT PERSON: a demise (priority.ts has already required a renowned person) that is carried by at least MAJOR_DEMISE_PAPERS different papers in at least two languages (an eminent person's death is told everywhere), or is that of a FORMER or sitting President, Prime Minister, Chief Minister, Governor, Chief Justice or Speaker, a Nobel or Bharat Ratna laureate, a pope (a bare "Prime Minister" in the headline is usually the one who condoles, so it is not enough);
- A HUGE LOSS OF LIFE: an accident or a massacre with at least MAJOR_DEAD dead;
- MANY PAPERS: any other priority story carried by at least MAJOR_PAPERS different papers, in at least two languages.
A major story is then shown in the tab of EVERY language that carried it (each its own earliest report), not only in the one where it arrived first. Any other story is still shown once.

symbols.name: isMajor
doc: Is this group of one event (its stories, from every language) major?

symbols.name: assignDesk
symbols.sig: export function assignDesk(items: DeskItem[], meaning?: (a: string, b: string) => boolean): Record<"en" | "hi" | "bn", DeskItem[]>
doc: ASSIGNS EACH STORY TO ONE LANGUAGE. `items` are the priority stories of the three languages together. The stories that are the same event (sameEvent, and a story that bridges two is one) form one group, which belongs to the language of the story that arrived FIRST; within that language the stories of the group are shown as one (the earliest-arrived headline of the language). Returns, for each language, the stories to show, in the order of the priority block: West Bengal, then India, then the world, the newest first within a scope.

behaviours: the death of a renowned person is found, in the three languages, and put in West Bengal, India or the world by the places it names
a death that is not a renowned person's stays an ordinary story: an ordinary man, a student, a suicide, a death toll, a film, a death penalty, 'will no longer remain' (नहीं रहेंगे)
a big accident is found: three or more dead, a word of disaster with a death, or any accident at a steel plant; in West Bengal first, else India
not covered: an accident abroad (Egypt, Kenya, Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, space), a small one, a crime, a market 'crash'
where: Bengal names (English, Hindi, Bengali) make West Bengal; a foreign name and no Indian one makes the world; Pakistan-occupied Kashmir is not India
the number of dead: digits, words, Hindi and Bengali digits and words, 'toll rises to 17', thousands with a comma
a name is the same in the three scripts: Dharmendra, धर्मेंद्र, ধর্মেন্দ্র; Chatterjee, चटर्जी; Soumitra, सौमित्र, সৌমিত্র; Bokaro, बोकारो, বোকারো
names of a headline: the capitalised Latin words and every Hindi or Bengali word, as skeletons of three consonants or more; the words of every headline (days, 'dies', 'minister') are not names

the death of an eminent person told by three papers in three languages is MAJOR: it stands in every one of the three tabs, each with its own language's report (the Bengali the earliest, 7 hours ago); another, lesser death stays in its one tab
a death told by only two papers is not major: it stands ONCE, in the tab of the language that arrived first (English, 9 hours ago); the Hindi report of it is left out
an accident told in three scripts is one story as well (the name of the place, and the same number of dead)
two different deaths on one day are never made one, nor a death and an accident
the same death of two days apart is not the same story (36 hours)
the block is in the order West Bengal, India, the world, the newest first inside a scope
the death of an eminent person told in three languages stands in all three tabs (it is major), each with its own report and flagged; the Bengali tab opens with it, in Bengali

the English tab opens with West Bengal's death (Kalyan Roy, Kolkata), then India's accident (Alwar, 3 killed) and India's other death (Dharmendra, major), newest first in the scope; all flagged, then the ordinary list in time order
the steel plant's accident is told in Hindi and Bengali: it stands ONCE, in the language that had it first (Bengali, 1 hour ago... no: Hindi, 2 hours ago, arrived before it) and not in the other
an ordinary headline of a tab that is not priority stays in its own tab's list
the priority block holds at most PRIORITY_CAP stories
when none of a tab's own feeds answers it is an error, whatever the other languages carry
a record of the market, gold, silver or the rupee that HAPPENED is found; a hope, a question, 'still below', a single company's stock, trading volume, futures and a cricket record are not

the Business tab opens with the RECORDS (the rupee's from the Economic Times' own feed, the Sensex's carried by two papers), flagged, newest first; a paper's lone claim (gold), a guess (Nifty eyes), and a record of four days ago (silver) are left out
the records stand first and the papers' own stories follow, none of them repeated (the rupee's record is not also an ordinary story)
share-price news of every other kind stays on the Business tab
the Business tab's sources are the four papers, then the record searches (fixed addresses of Google News and Bing News)
when no record search answers, the engines are named as not answering and the papers' own stories still show
a diplomatic visit is told in the three languages: the Prime Minister abroad (scope world), a foreign leader or delegation in India (scope india)

what is not a diplomatic visit stays ordinary: a domestic rally, border post or temple, a phone or video call, a foreign visit that does not involve India's Prime Minister or India, a cricket team, Nirav Modi, India Gate, a domestic visitor
a death or an accident is still itself even when a visit is named (a demise comes first), and a visit does not take a death's place
one visit told in English, Hindi and Bengali is shown once: in the English tab, where it arrived first
two different visits are two stories
a mass killing with a large toll (10 or more dead) is a MASSACRE, wherever in the world, in the three languages; its scope is where it happened
what is not a mass killing is not a massacre: fewer than ten dead, a film or a game, an accident (which stays an accident)
an accident is still an accident and a massacre a massacre (a bomb blast attack is not an accident)
a huge massacre (25 or more dead) told in two languages by two papers stands in BOTH tabs (major by its toll); a smaller one (12 dead) stands once, where it arrived first
the death of a former Prime Minister is major whatever the number of papers: in every tab that carried it; a PM who only CONDOLES (the actor's death) does not make a death major
a story carried by six or more papers in two or more languages is major, whatever its kind (a visit that every paper tells)
a major story shows in a language only once even when that language has several reports of it (its earliest, naming the other papers)
the watch looks every three minutes, not oftener
the first look only learns what is there (nothing is 'new' at the start), even when priority headlines are among them
after that, a new death, massacre, accident or visit is reported as new once; an ordinary headline, or one already seen, is not
